A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OLM research despite different titles and formatting. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-data, MNIST and CelebA experiments, including reconstruction scores, measurement analyses and appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original image experiments and reports additional synthetic, ICA and measurement-distribution results.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the denoiser prior, constrained sampling, posterior-mean approximation and Householder-parameterized measurement optimization. The MSE and SSIM objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a synthetic reconstruction scenario involving a closed, curved one-dimensional manifold in Figure 1. MNIST, CelebA and the Gaussian and sparse synthetic coverage remain.

E2.justification: V2 newly reports evaluating ICA measurements on both image datasets in Section 3.3 and includes ICA in Figure 4F's mutual-information comparison. The existing PCA, random-measurement and Table 1 comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 4E–F introduces component-wise skewness evaluation and mutual-information distributions across all pairs of measurement directions. Appendix E retains the existing splits, preprocessing, training budgets and posterior-sampling settings.

E4.justification: V2 extends measurement characterization with analyses of asymmetry and pairwise dependence, and adds the curved-manifold reconstruction illustration. V1's supplementary Gaussian-ridge toy analysis is removed. Existing variance, subspace-distance and perceptual-loss analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same standard-error reporting. V2 adds no independent-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: V2 adds curved-manifold results, greater OLM skewness than PCA, higher pairwise mutual information than PCA/ICA, and the qualitative finding that ICA performs marginally worse than PCs. Toy reconstruction plots are revised and the old supplementary Gaussian-ridge results disappear. Main image results remain unchanged, including the 4.72 dB MNIST and 0.44 dB CelebA peak advantages, Figure 5's SSIM values and Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16, the Tweedie/Miyasawa and PCA derivations, and the noise-free and orthonormal-measurement assumptions are retained. No new formal result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract newly highlights asymmetric measurement distributions, and the abstract/introduction extend the claimed distinction from classical measurements to ICA. The central contributions concerning optimized measurements, reconstruction quality and dataset/loss dependence remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly interprets skewness and increased pairwise mutual information as evidence of asymmetric, dependent measurement distributions, linking them to non-axis-aligned structure. The computational, measurement-noise and physical-constraint limitations in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E retain the same implementation, architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes and sampling details; code-access information is unchanged. V2 supplies no corresponding implementation details for ICA or mutual-information estimation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hyvärinen and Oja (2000) for ICA and application references by Pruessmann, Nehme and Zhu. It removes the earlier introduction's general inverse-problem and specific image-restoration references. The substantive related-work discussion is otherwise largely retained.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on the title, abstract, introductory framing and expanded two-dimensional explanation. Section 3.4 is renamed, acknowledgments disappear and citations become author–year. Overall section order and most technical and appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: The document is extensively restyled through typography, margins, headings, author layout and figure placement. Figure 1 changes from two rows and four columns to three rows and three columns, with explicit conditional samples; denoiser fields move to Supplementary Figure 1. Figure 4 gains panels E–F.

improvement.justification: V2 improves characterization beyond v1's variance and subspace comparisons through the skewness/mutual-information analyses and ICA check. The curved-manifold example and explicit sample-versus-mean display also improve explanation. These are limited gains: ICA reconstruction performance remains qualitative, and mutual-information estimation is undocumented, while the main benchmark evidence remains intact.
